note: The recorded run of one real content path: the served completion of the marking suite fetched by a client, rendered and exported by a browser, read back out of the archive by two text extractors and by an optical engine, and attempted through a media remux. Each stage names the application and the version that produced its bytes, and a stage with no bytes is one that did not run, for which the vectors built from this file state no outcome. Where an install sits on a machine is not stated here.

stages.name: client-fetch-to-file
stages.note: The served body written to a file by a real client over a loopback socket: the copying step, which moves the bytes and changes none of them.

stages.name: browser-rendered-document
stages.note: The same file opened in the browser and serialized as the document it renders, so the region has to survive markup wrapped around it.

stages.name: browser-exported-pdf
stages.note: That rendered page exported to PDF by the browser with its page header and footer off, which is the archive a customer keeps.

stages.name: pdf-text-export
stages.note: The text one extractor takes back out of that archive, which is what a reader holds when they copy the page out of the PDF.

stages.name: pdf-text-export-second-application
stages.note: The same archive read by a second application, so the answer above is not one extractor spacing the page differently.

stages.name: pdf-page-raster-ocr-text
stages.note: The page rasterized by Artifex Ghostscript at 150 dots per inch and read by an optical engine, which is the text a scan of the printed page turns into.

stages.name: office-document-export
stages.note: Named as a step of this path and not run: no office suite was installed where the path was measured, so nothing is stated about what one does to the region.

stages.name: media-container-transcode
stages.note: Named as a step of this path and not run: FFmpeg 2025-09-04-git-2611874a50-full_build-www.gyan.dev reads no media stream out of these bytes and answered "[tedcaptions @ 0000011ac0ae6bc0] Syntax error near offset 7.", so no transcoded bytes exist and no outcome is stated for the step.
